book.prscraft.workflow.title: Devices and cabling
book.prscraft.workflow.body: TX generates a signal; RX receives the source automatically. Connect matching ports and cable on each side. Orange/back is the input of an active processor; green/front is its output. Loss is measured in dB. The RF carrier in MHz identifies the channel and affects cable attenuation; it is separate from the displayed waveform frequencies in Hz.
book.prscraft.functions.title: Sines and cosines
book.prscraft.functions.body: Write a sum such as sin(10)+0.5*cos(20). Up to eight terms are supported. Numbers in parentheses are Hz, not radians/second. Each term and the sum have independently visible graph layers. Apply commits settings to the server; a preview edit alone does not alter the device.
book.prscraft.sampling.title: Sampling I and II
book.prscraft.sampling.body: I: a pulse gate passes the changing waveform while open. II: the value at pulse start is held until the pulse ends. Duty sets the open fraction. Outside pulses the output is zero. The sample rate must be at least twice the highest nonzero source frequency; invalid settings are rejected on both client and server.
book.prscraft.quantization.title: Quantization
book.prscraft.quantization.body: Quantization follows sampling. Choose 2–4096 uniform levels. Endpoints are ±sum of absolute source amplitudes. Even level counts may not contain zero. Quantization, pulse gating, cable loss and noise explain why the received waveform can differ from the initial sine. Analog mode bypasses sampling and quantization.
book.prscraft.digital.title: Bits and discrete sequences
book.prscraft.digital.body: TX can output NRZ bits or an explicit sample list. Repeat makes a periodic signal; one-shot returns zero outside the finite sequence. Preview offset selects a later window. Bernoulli bits use P1 with P0=1−P1, configurable A0/A1 and a reproducible seed. The separate bit-generator block is a convenient source of the same signal; TX can do it too. Mode buttons always show their current mode; hover for the full name. Choose UNRZ/URZ line coding in Source / AWGN.
book.prscraft.processors.title: Amplifier and filter
book.prscraft.processors.body: Amplifier gain is −40…60 dB with clipping at ±16 u. The frequency filter is an ideal FFT bandpass over a finite periodic window, not a physical circuit with memory. Low=0 makes a low-pass. Filter boundaries are waveform Hz, not RF MHz. Window edges can produce leakage/ringing. Processing order matters.
book.prscraft.modulation.title: AM and BPSK
book.prscraft.modulation.body: AM varies the carrier envelope. BPSK holds a symbol and multiplies it by a cosine. Opposite equal levels −A,+A produce true antipodal BPSK; unequal magnitudes produce a more general amplitude/phase binary signal. Match bit and symbol rates. The coherent RX decoder assumes known frequency, phase and symbol timing; it does not acquire synchronization automatically.
book.prscraft.gaussian.title: Gaussian noise and normalization
book.prscraft.gaussian.body: AWGN adds a mean plus a scaled standard Gaussian draw. Variance is the square of standard deviation, not RMS when mean is nonzero. Normalized Z subtracts the mean and divides by sigma. In the lab, normalization changes displayed coordinates and thresholds, not physical channel samples or error probability. At zero variance noise is deterministic and Z is undefined.
book.prscraft.awgn.title: AWGN, priors and MAP
book.prscraft.awgn.body: The lab runs 10000 scalar binary trials with the selected levels, priors, Gaussian mean and variance. Conditional means are mi=Ai+mu. MAP includes the prior ratio and minimizes error for this model. Extreme priors always select the certain symbol. The Q prediction is for symbol space, not an exact BER claim for arbitrary clipping, filtering or RF chains.
book.prscraft.q.title: Q-function and tail approximation
book.prscraft.q.body: Q is the standard-normal upper-tail probability. For x≤3 a normal-CDF polynomial is used; above 3 a 64-level continued-fraction Mills-ratio approximation avoids cancellation in the tiny tail. Negative arguments use Q(−x)=1−Q(x). The classic BPSK formula assumes equal priors, opposite equal-energy symbols and a properly normalized coherent detector.
book.prscraft.spectrum.title: Spectrum and PSD
book.prscraft.spectrum.body: Open Spectrum from a device, saved capture or analyzer. Select source output, channel input or RX; switch amplitude/PSD/ESD and linear/dB. This is a one-sided rectangular periodogram. Double interior bins only: DC and Nyquist are unique. The preview sample rate is N/T and differs from configured ADC fvz. Finite windows cause leakage; noise PSD is a noisy estimate, not an exactly flat line.
book.prscraft.energy.title: Power W and energy J
book.prscraft.energy.body: One amplitude unit squared references 0.1 W. Lab W normalizes average source power before ADC; later processing can change it. J is allowed only for a finite nonrandom, nonrepeating bit/sample sequence and refers to the entire sequence. Spectrum P/E cover only its captured window. Periodic infinite-duration signals have infinite energy. ESD is J/Hz, PSD is W/Hz; both obey Parseval. Integrator and raw correlation outputs change dimensions; W/J spectra are disabled for them instead of falsely treating them as power amplitudes. Their sourceOutput spectrum remains available.
book.prscraft.presets.title: Identifiable templates
book.prscraft.presets.body: Apply settings, open Templates/recordings, insert paper and save. Colored headers and diagrams distinguish TX, RX, amplifier, filter, modulator and bit generator. The item name and hover text include real values. Insert into the same device type to restore settings and graph layers. Old templates still load; resaving refreshes their name. Anvil names are not overwritten. DSP templates also save A/B gains, timing, lag and correlation-view preferences.
book.prscraft.recordings.title: Recording and CSV
book.prscraft.recordings.body: A data card stores a fresh 512-sample snapshot, settings and channel metadata. Recording overwrites that card; it is not a continuous logger. Saved captures reopen read-only and can be analyzed in Spectrum. CSV is written to the client game directory under prscraft/recordings with unique filenames. A frozen UI is not an archive: use a card to preserve exact samples. Spectrum CSV exports frequency, amplitude, PSD and ESD. Correlator cards preserve input B, lag correlation and its peak.
book.prscraft.analyzer.title: Analyzer without chat spam
book.prscraft.analyzer.body: The read-only analyzer now surveys the whole connected circuit, including active devices and every port. Use list pages or the circuit map, select a device and inspect its waveform, spectral data or CSV. A/B/OUT labels explain direction. Scope and bounds are explicit: 1024 physical nodes, 32 listed devices, 128 bus edges. Reading never reconfigures devices. Hold the analyzer and remain near the clicked port for updates.
book.prscraft.limits.title: Simulation limits and maintenance
book.prscraft.limits.body: This is a bounded finite-window simulator. Active branches are evaluated recursively on one common grid; each cable segment attenuates and adds damage noise before the next device. RX adds its own AWGN/thermal noise. Passive loops use shortest weighted routes, not reflected or summed electromagnetic waves. Active feedback is rejected. Limits: 512 passive nodes per route search, 16 active depth, 32 unique devices, 256 evaluation attempts. No propagation field solver or automatic synchronization.

book.prscraft.circuit.title: Whole-circuit topology
book.prscraft.circuit.body: The analyzer crosses active devices and counts every connected port and cable. Its map shows passive buses between devices, not only the segment you clicked. Select any of up to 32 devices; list pages show eight at once. Physical connectivity is undirected; signal computation follows A/B into OUT. Unused-side ports can be visible without being valid signal inputs. Feedback graphs are reported, not solved as oscillators. All blocks use original PRSCraft textures: named waveform panels; input A is orange, B blue, OUT green.
book.prscraft.math_blocks.title: Adder and integrator
book.prscraft.math_blocks.body: Adder input A is behind the block, B is on its left, OUT is in front. Both input gains are adjustable; a negative B gain subtracts. Sources are evaluated on the same 512-point grid. The integrator uses trapezoids from the start of each capture until T, then holds the result. It resets for each window, not each game tick. Integration changes dimensions: u becomes u·s. Adding incompatible dimensions is rejected.
book.prscraft.correlation.title: Correlation and delay peak
book.prscraft.correlation.body: The correlator has the same A/B/OUT orientation as the adder. Cross mode needs both inputs; auto mode uses A twice. Its time output is the running integral of A·B, optionally normalized. Switch to R(lag) to see zero-padded cross-correlation and the signed peak lag. Positive peak lag means B is delayed relative to A. Global energy normalization bounds coefficients by ±1; zero-energy inputs give zero. Periodic signals can have ambiguous peaks. T limits the running time integral; R(lag) uses the complete captured window.
book.prscraft.timing.title: Timed gate and delay line
book.prscraft.timing.body: The gate closes electrically in the signal model at t=T. Hold mode passes all later samples; pulse mode passes only [T,T+width). These times are relative to the capture window, not the Minecraft clock or a redstone timer. Delay uses fractional-sample linear interpolation and zeros outside the captured signal. It never wraps the end to the beginning. The extra delay block lets you check that a correlator recovers a known shift, preferably with a nonperiodic bit pattern.
book.prscraft.cables.title: Cable wrench and damage
book.prscraft.cables.body: Right-click cable with the calibration wrench. Set its effective length to 0.01–1000 m and damage to 0–100%. The model stays one block long. Settings survive world reload; newly placed cable starts at 1 m and zero damage. Damage adds attenuation and equivalent Gaussian noise at that segment before the next processor, so an amplifier also amplifies this noise. These are teaching coefficients, not real cable specifications. Total cable metres are distinct from path metrics, which also count fixed 1 m port/device hops.
book.prscraft.advancements.title: Laboratory advancements
book.prscraft.advancements.body: Obtain the handbook, establish a valid RX link, calibrate a cable, compute a connected correlation, survey a circuit of three or more devices, and obtain an adder/integrator. Action achievements are granted by successful operations rather than merely holding the block. Toasts are enabled without public chat announcements. Open the Minecraft advancements screen to follow the laboratory tree. There are also 9 new circuit and board goals; challenge pages explain exact conditions and examples. Nine more goals cover fiber, copper, 100 metres, four tones, gain, subtraction, autocorrelation, a deep chain and a large canvas.
book.prscraft.workflow.symbols: TX: source; RX: receiver; A: amplitude; Ptx: dBm; loss: dB. Match RF MHz on TX and RX.
book.prscraft.functions.symbols: t: seconds; f: Hz; A/B: amplitudes; Σ: sum of terms; π ≈ 3.14159. A 10 Hz tone repeats every 0.1 s.
book.prscraft.sampling.symbols: fvz: samples/s; fmax: highest tone; Ts: sample interval; τ: pulse width; duty=τ/Ts. A 20 Hz tone needs at least 40 samples/s; try 100.
book.prscraft.quantization.symbols: L: level count; Amax: sum of absolute amplitudes; Δ: spacing; round: nearest integer. Amax=1, L=5 gives −1, −0.5, 0, 0.5, 1.
book.prscraft.digital.symbols: P: probability; p=P(1); A0/A1: symbol levels; Rb: bit/s; Tb: bit duration. With p=0.8, about 80% of a long sequence are ones.
book.prscraft.processors.symbols: GdB: gain in dB; gain: amplitude multiplier; k: FFT bin; T: window seconds. +6 dB is approximately ×2 amplitude; +20 dB is ×10.
book.prscraft.modulation.symbols: fc: waveform carrier Hz; m: AM depth; peak: max |x|; b: bit level. For Rb=10 bit/s try fc=100 Hz. RF MHz is a separate setting.
book.prscraft.gaussian.symbols: μ: mean; σ: standard deviation; σ²: variance; Z: standard normal noise. μ=0 and variance=0.04 gives σ=RMS=0.2.
book.prscraft.awgn.symbols: Ai: symbol level; mi=Ai+μ: received mean; P0/P1: priors; η: decision threshold; ln: natural logarithm; Pe: error probability.
book.prscraft.q.symbols: x: distance from threshold in σ; φ(x)=exp(−x²/2)/sqrt(2π); Eb: bit energy; N0: noise density. Q(0)=0.5; Q(3)≈0.00135.
book.prscraft.spectrum.symbols: N=512 samples; dt=T/N; k: bin index; c=2 for interior bins, 1 for DC/Nyquist; j²=−1. T=1 s gives 1 Hz bin spacing.
book.prscraft.energy.symbols: P: watts; E: joules; T: window seconds; mean(x²): mean square; Δf: bin width. x=1 for 2 s gives P=0.1 W and E=0.2 J.
book.prscraft.presets.symbols: A template stores settings, not samples. Apply first, put paper in the media slot and save a template. Insert it into a compatible device.
book.prscraft.recordings.symbols: A sample is one value at one instant. The 512 points form a finite window. CSV opens in spreadsheets/Python; the card preserves that capture including noise.
book.prscraft.analyzer.symbols: A/B: inputs; OUT: output; TX/RX: radio role. A map edge is a passive bus, not one cable block. Select a device in the list or map.
book.prscraft.circuit.symbols: Example: TX → port → amplifier A; amplifier OUT → port → RX. Orient every processor correctly; unused sides do not become inputs.
book.prscraft.math_blocks.symbols: gA/gB: input multipliers; ∫: accumulated area; T: stop time; s: seconds. A constant x=2 for 0.5 s integrates to 1 u·s before cable losses.
book.prscraft.correlation.symbols: τ: time shift; R: raw correlation; ρ: normalized coefficient from −1 to 1. Delaying B by 0.02 s should move the peak near +0.02 s.
book.prscraft.timing.symbols: t: time inside the capture; T: opening time; width: duration; D: delay. T=0.2 and width=0.1 passes samples from 0.2 to 0.3 s.
book.prscraft.cables.symbols: L: effective metres; d: damage fraction 0…1. L=0.25 m and d=0.5 adds 0.375 dB loss. These are educational coefficients.
book.prscraft.advancements.symbols: Use Minecraft’s Advancements menu for the tree. Challenge pages describe new goals. Open the final RX or relevant processor to validate a circuit.
book.prscraft.limits.symbols: A shared window aligns all branches. Game time is not signal time; each capture recomputes integrators. Board drawings persist independently of signal captures.
book.prscraft.line_coding.title: Unipolar UNRZ and URZ
book.prscraft.line_coding.body: On TX choose Bits, then Source / AWGN → line code. UNRZ holds +A throughout a one; URZ holds +A only for the duty fraction, then returns to zero. Zero always maps to zero; A0 is ignored, A1=A>0. Set URZ duty on the main panel. On RX select the matching decoder and Rb/duty. In the RX lab, A1 is the expected received amplitude after losses. The decision compares the active-bit average to A1/2. Timing is coherent, without automatic synchronization.
book.prscraft.line_coding.symbols: Example: 1010, Rb=10, A=1, duty=0.5. URZ is +1 from 0 to 0.05 s, zero until 0.2 s, +1 from 0.2 to 0.25 s. W/J normalization includes duty.
book.prscraft.drawing.title: Board, chalk and eraser
book.prscraft.drawing.body: Place a board and right-click holding chalk or an eraser. The same drawing is visible in the editor and on the block to everyone, surviving reloads and moving the board. Choose brush size 1/2/4/8/16 and the tool hand. Without a tool the board is read-only. Chalk breaks after 4096 touched pixels. The eraser spends 16384 uses including blank pixels, but remains when empty. Right-click a water cauldron to restore it, consuming one water level. Calcite crafts 4 chalk; bone meal crafts 1. Chalk plus any dye changes its color while preserving wear. Eraser: white wool + stick.
book.prscraft.drawing.symbols: One 8×8 dab spends 64 durability; pixels outside the board do not count. Color comes from the held chalk item, not a free palette. One eraser clears a complete 128×128 board; legacy erasers retain pixels already spent and receive the new capacity.
book.prscraft.challenges.title: How challenges work
book.prscraft.challenges.body: Challenges are checked by the server against a working connected circuit. Apply settings, then open the final RX or relevant processor. Owning the blocks is insufficient. Missing inputs, mismatched carriers and disconnected links do not count. The Reception and Mathematics challenge pages list exact conditions. For Colorful notes, paint at least 256 pixels using three colors. For Second chance, spend all 16384 eraser uses and wash it in a cauldron.
book.prscraft.challenges.symbols: 38 advancements total. Basic goals: handbook, first RX, cable calibration, correlation, survey of ≥3 devices, owning an adder/integrator. Toasts do not announce to chat.
book.prscraft.challenges_rx.title: Challenges: reception
book.prscraft.challenges_rx.body: Microlink: working RX with at least one cable and total effective cable length below 1 m. Unipolar link: transmit a fixed pattern containing zero and one without a time offset; matching UNRZ/URZ RX must correctly decode at least 4 bits. Through noise: correctly decode ≥4 bits through a BPSK modulator with RX noise variance ≥0.0001. Start with 10110010, Rb=10, fc=100. Frequency selection: open a connected filter with nonzero output energy below 25% of input energy. Try sin(10)+3*cos(80) through a 0–20 Hz band.
book.prscraft.challenges_rx.symbols: Loss changes received amplitude: A_RX=A_TX·10^(−loss/20). Match duty for URZ, fc/Rb for BPSK. Bit challenges require a nonrandom source.
book.prscraft.challenges_math.title: Challenges: mathematics
book.prscraft.challenges_math.body: Area of a sum: connect two TX sources to adder A/B, then its OUT to integrator A. Open the integrator: the working pipeline must include both blocks and have u·s output. Integration window: TX → time gate → integrator; choose T inside the capture and obtain nonzero area. Delay hunter: feed the same bit pattern directly to correlator A and through a delay line to B. Disable autocorrelation and enable normalization. Require |peak lag| ≥0.005 s and peak coefficient >0.9. Try D=0.02 s and lag range 0.1 s.
book.prscraft.challenges_math.symbols: Use compatible ports on intermediate links. Processor A is at the back, B at the left, OUT at the front. Signals with incompatible units cannot be added.

book.prscraft.learning_tx.title: Learning: TX settings
book.prscraft.learning_tx.body: Apply each change on TX, then open the connected RX. Without steps: analog mode. Sample by sample: sampled mode. Steps of levels: quantized; Eight bits of levels: L≥256. Natural sampling / Hold the value: first / second kind in sampled or quantized mode. Compare pulse shapes at duty=0.5. A biased coin: random bits with 0.75≤P1<1. One burst: bits or a discrete list, random and repeat disabled. Later in time: set a positive source offset and receive nonzero output.
book.prscraft.learning_tx.symbols: fvz must satisfy Nyquist. Higher L reduces quantization spacing, not channel noise. An offset beyond a finite sequence produces zero output.
book.prscraft.learning_rx.title: Learning: RX and W/J
book.prscraft.learning_rx.body: The one level / Return to zero: correctly receive ≥4 UNRZ / URZ bits containing zero and one; fixed source, offset zero. Match Rb and URZ duty; RX A1 must account for losses. Quiet laboratory: disable RX thermal noise, set mean and variance to zero and receive nonzero output. This does not disable damaged-cable noise. Set the watts: source quantity W with target >0. Count the joules: quantity J with target >0, finite nonrandom bits/list with repeat disabled. Open Spectrum and compare the target with captured-window P/E.
book.prscraft.learning_rx.symbols: Goals confirm settings on a working circuit, not an ideal received value: losses and processing change P/E. 38 advancements total; existing progress is retained.
